title: Politeness, requests & invitations
goal: Ask favours politely, invite people and respond to invitations, offer and refuse, and use the most respectful forms with elders.
intro:
Nepali politeness lives in the **verb**. The same request can be blunt (दे 'give!'), friendly (देऊ), polite (दिनुहोस्), extra-gentle (दिनुहुन्छ कि?) or even royal (दिइबक्सियोस्). In this unit you'll learn to make requests that sound natural, especially with the 'for me' form **-इदिनु**: लेखिदिनुहोस् 'please write it (for me)'.

You'll also learn 'let's' (**जाऔँ**), 'shall I?' (**म गरूँ?**), blessings (**सफल होस्**), and how to handle a Nepali host who keeps refilling your plate.

vocab.note: Key word for polite refusals: आज अलि अप्ठ्यारो छ.
संकोच नमान्नुहोस् 'don't hold back / make yourself at home'.
ढोग्नु / ढोग गर्नु 'to bow to an elder'.
दर्शन गर्न आएँ 'I've come to pay my respects'.
Used for highly respected people: खाना पाल्नुहोस् 'please eat'.

vocab.en: to offer (to a deity); to put up
small gift (brought when visiting or from a trip)

phrases.en: Could you come here a moment?
Could you do me a favour?
Could you write this down for me?
Sit down — have some tea before you go.

phrases.native: हाम्रो घरमा खाना खान आउनुहोस् न।
phrases.roman: hāmro gharmā khānā khāna āunuhos na.
phrases.en: Do come and eat at our house.

phrases.native: आज अलि अप्ठ्यारो छ, अर्को पटक है।
phrases.roman: āja ali apṭhyāro chha, arko paṭak hai.
phrases.en: Today's a bit difficult — another time, OK?
Don't be shy — make yourself at home.
You shouldn't have! (when given a gift)
phrases.note: Lit. 'why did you take the trouble?'

grammar.title: Making requests sound natural
grammar.body:
A ladder of politeness for 'give' (दिनु):

**दे** (तँ) → **देऊ** (तिमी) → **दिनुहोस् / दिनुस्** (तपाईं) → **दिनुहोस् न** (softened) → **दिनुहुन्छ?** / **दिनुहुन्छ कि?** 'would you give?' → **दिन सक्नुहुन्छ?** 'could you give?' → **दिनुहोला** 'please (do) give' → **दिइबक्सियोस्** (royal/very formal).

The most natural-sounding trick is the **'for me' form -इदिनु** (stem + -इ + दिनु). It shows the action is a favour to someone: **लेखिदिनुहोस्** 'please write it for me', **ढोका खोलिदिनुहोस्** 'please open the door (for me)', **एकछिन हेरिदिनुहोस्** 'please keep an eye on it for a moment'. Vowel stems: ल्याइदिनु, पढिदिनु.

For a request meant for later, तिमी has a 'deferred' imperative in **-नू**: तिमी भोलि **आउनू** है 'do come tomorrow'.

examples.en: Give me some water, would you? (तिमी)
Could you read this letter for me?

grammar.title: Let's…, shall I…?, may it be…
grammar.body:
**Let's** (हामी): stem + **-औँ**: **जाऔँ** 'let's go', **खाऔँ** 'let's eat', **गरौँ** 'let's do', **बसौँ** 'let's sit'. Negative: **नजाऔँ** 'let's not go'.

**Shall I? / May I?** (म): stem + **-ऊँ**: **म जाऊँ?** 'shall I go? / may I go?', **गरूँ?** 'shall I do it?', **खाऊँ?**, **दिऊँ?**. With पाउनु it asks permission: **आउन पाऊँ?** 'may I come in?'.

**May he/she/it…** (3rd person wish): stem + **-ओस्**: **ऊ आओस्** 'let him come', and in blessings and wishes with हुनु → **होस्**: **सफल होस्** 'may you succeed', **चाँडै निको होस्** 'get well soon', **दीर्घायु होस्** 'may you live long'. For तपाईं the wish form is **-नुहोस्**: सधैँ खुसी रहनुहोस् 'may you always be happy'.

examples.en: May God bless you (lit. do good).

grammar.title: Offering, accepting and refusing
grammar.body:
Nepali hosts **insist**, and guests are expected to refuse at least once. A host saying **लिनुहोस् न, संकोच नमान्नुहोस्** 'take some, don't be shy' will keep going until you firmly but warmly say **पुग्यो** 'enough' or **पेट भरियो** 'I'm full', ideally with your hand over your plate.

Accepting: **हुन्छ, धन्यवाद** · **खुसीसाथ** · **अलिकति मात्र** 'just a little'.
Refusing gently: **पर्दैन, धन्यवाद** 'no need, thanks' · **आज अलि अप्ठ्यारो छ** 'today's a bit difficult' · **अर्को पटक** 'next time' · **हेरौँ** 'let's see'. A direct **होइन** or **हुँदैन** sounds harsh in this context.

With very respected people, verbs like **पाल्नुहोस्** (come/eat), **बक्सनुहोस्** or the -इबक्सियोस् form appear — you need to recognise them, rarely to produce them.

examples.en: Shall I give you a little more rice?
No thanks, that's enough. Thank you.

dialogue.title: Dinner with Sita's family
dialogue.setting: Sita invites Sarah home. The next evening Sarah meets Sita's mother, who treats her like a daughter and uses तिमी with her.

lines.speaker: Sita
lines.native: सारा, भोलि बेलुका हाम्रो घरमा खाना खान आउनुहोस् न।
lines.roman: Sārā, bholi belukā hāmro gharmā khānā khāna āunuhos na.
lines.en: Sarah, do come and eat at our house tomorrow evening.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: निम्तोको लागि धन्यवाद! तपाईंलाई अप्ठ्यारो त हुँदैन?
lines.roman: nimtoko lāgi dhanyabād! tapāiṃlāi apṭhyāro ta huṃdaina?
lines.en: Thanks for the invitation! It won't be any trouble for you?

lines.speaker: Sita
lines.native: कत्ति हुँदैन! आमाले पनि बोलाउनुभएको छ।
lines.roman: katti huṃdaina! āmāle pani bolāunubhaeko chha.
lines.en: Not at all! My mother invited you too.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: नमस्ते आमा! मैले अलिकति मिठाई ल्याएँ।
lines.roman: namaste āmā! maile alikati miṭhāi lyāeṃ.
lines.en: Namaste, mother! I've brought a few sweets.

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.native: किन दुःख गरेकी, नानी? आऊ, बस।
lines.roman: kina dukha gareki, nāni? āu, basa.
lines.en: Oh, you shouldn't have, dear! Come, sit.

lines.speaker: Sita
lines.en: Right, shall I serve the food?

lines.speaker: Mother
lines.native: पाहुनालाई अलिकति कहाँ हुन्छ! संकोच नमान, अझ लेऊ।
lines.roman: pāhunālāi alikati kahāṃ hunchha! sankoch namāna, ajha leu.
lines.en: A guest can't have just a little! Don't be shy, take some more.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.native: पुग्यो आमा, पेट भरियो। खाना एकदम मिठो थियो।
lines.roman: pugyo āmā, peṭ bhariyo. khānā ekdam miṭho thiyo.
lines.en: That's enough, mother, I'm full. The food was really delicious.

lines.speaker: Sarah
lines.en: I certainly will. Thank you, mother!

culture: **अतिथि देवो भव** — 'the guest is a god' — is taken seriously in Nepal: you'll be fed generously and urged to eat more. Give and receive things with the **right hand** (or both hands, or the right hand with the left touching your right forearm) as a sign of respect. Gifts are usually not opened in front of the giver. Younger relatives greet elders, especially at Dashain, with **ढोग** (bowing to touch their feet) and receive **आशीर्वाद** (blessings) in return. It's also normal for an older woman to call a young female guest **नानी** or **छोरी** and switch to तिमी — a sign of warmth, not disrespect.
